items.claim: The row's opening seam rests on a verse-initial subordinating particle whose byte function argues continuity backward across that very cut, and its closing seam carries an undisclosed servant-root catchword hook.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.14.1 opens with כִּי֩ (byte tier), a subordinating particle whose clause supplies the ground for the announcement that ends oshb:Isa.13.22 at  (byte tier) — so the one positive Hebrew signal standing at the cut is a device that links across it, and the row nowhere discloses that continuity reading. Nothing in the prophetic frame spine sits at Isa.14.1: over the whole span Isa.14.1-Isa.16.12 the frame sites are 2 verses carrying the burden-word (Isa.14.28 mid-verse, Isa.15.1 verse-initial), 2 verses carrying the postpositive oracle signature (Isa.14.22, Isa.14.23), 1 non-initial woe-family token (Isa.16.4), and zero verses with the messenger-formula frame, zero with divine-speech-verb adjacency, zero with the Holy-One-of-Israel title. The parashah layer is likewise silent at Isa.13.22|Isa.14.1 and marks Isa.14.2 instead (SAMEKH seg standing after that verse's words in the single witness, tier-3), so the corroboration the row cites belongs to its close, not its open. At that close the servant root recurs immediately across the cut: oshb:Isa.14.2 carries לַעֲבָדִ֖ים (byte tier), and oshb:Isa.14.3 carries both הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה and עֻבַּד (byte tier) — a catchword hook straddling the row's own seam that neither this row nor the following one discloses.

items.claim: The frame-plus-speech unit is byte-sound: the temporal clause and the frame verb form one syntactic period, the demonstrative is cataphoric to the speech it introduces, and the disclosure layers owe nothing inside the span.
items.evidence: וְנָשָׂ֜אתָ opens oshb:Isa.14.4 (byte tier) as a waw-consecutive perfect continuing the וְהָיָ֗ה protasis that opens oshb:Isa.14.3 (byte tier); the two verses are therefore one period and the cut lands after it rather than inside it, which is what the row argues. The demonstrative phrase הַמָּשָׁ֥ל הַזֶּ֛ה at oshb:Isa.14.4 (byte tier) points forward to the taunt it introduces, matching the frame-plus-speech treatment; the row's opening splice sits verse-initial at its cited ref. The opening seam is corroborated single-witness at tier-3 by the SAMEKH seg standing after Isa.14.2, correctly typed and never conflated with petuchah. Across Isa.14.3-Isa.14.21 no parashah seg, no ketiv/qere note and no special-letter seg falls inside the span (the nearest variant-note verses are Isa.13.16 and Isa.16.3), so no disclosure object is left owed. The row's own statement that the close at Isa.14.21 rests on content rather than a formal marker is byte-accurate: no frame device stands at Isa.14.21, and the next one is the postpositive signature inside the following verse.

items.claim: The bracket conclusion survives the bytes, but the run quoted as the unit's closing evidence is not verse-final, and the signature count-object is mis-specified.
items.evidence: The row cites וְטֵֽאטֵאתִ֨יהָ֙ בְּמַטְאֲטֵ֣א הַשְׁמֵ֔ד (byte tier) as ending oshb:Isa.14.23, but those are the sixth through eighth of that verse's eleven tokens; the verse actually ends נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (byte tier) — the very signature the row's whole bracket argument rests on, so the closing evidence quotes past the device and stops short of it. The signature census over the couplet is three tokens across two verses, not two. At oshb:Isa.14.22 the signature stands twice: נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת postpositive to that verse's opening clause, and verse-finally in that same oshb:Isa.14.22, נְאֻם יְהוָֽה — a bare-tetragrammaton stack with no hosts-title. At oshb:Isa.14.23 the closing stack is נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (all byte tier). The two verse-final stacks agree in their first two consonantal tokens but are NOT byte-identical, the hosts-title standing only at oshb:Isa.14.23 — a skeleton-grade reading collapses them where the pointed bytes keep them apart. Naming the object as a doubled hosts-title signature therefore leaves the third token and its distinct title stack unnamed, against the rule that divine-name citations name the exact stack they count. The device is also postpositive rather than an onset: at oshb:Isa.14.22 it follows וְקַמְתִּ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם (byte tier), so the couplet is signature-closed at both ends, not signature-opened. The PE seg standing after Isa.14.23 is correctly typed and single-witness-disclosed.

items.claim: The oath-formula onset, the named pivot and both petuchah citations are byte-true and correctly typed, and the row stays clear of the stretched-hand refrain trap.
items.evidence: נִשְׁבַּ֛ע יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר stands verse-initial at oshb:Isa.14.24 (byte tier) and is a frame device distinct in form from the postpositive signature closing the preceding couplet, so the row's separation of the two is byte-grounded. The pivot the row names is byte-present: לִשְׁבֹּ֤ר אַשּׁוּר֙ בְּאַרְצִ֔י at oshb:Isa.14.25 and עַל כָּל הָאָ֑רֶץ at oshb:Isa.14.26 (byte tier). Both marks the row cites are petuchah and both are correctly located — PE segs stand after Isa.14.23 and after Isa.14.27 in the single witness (tier-3, never conflated with setumah). The stretched-hand wording the row quotes in English at its close is NOT the book's stretched-hand refrain: הַיָּ֥ד הַנְּטוּיָ֖ה at oshb:Isa.14.26 and וְיָד֥וֹ הַנְּטוּיָ֖ה at oshb:Isa.14.27 (byte tier) differ in wording from the refrain, whose byte-identical sites number 5 verses, none of them in chs 14-16; and because both stretched-hand verses sit inside this row's own span there is no undisclosed straddle. No ketiv/qere note, paseq seg or special-letter seg falls inside Isa.14.24-Isa.14.27; the two PE segs the row cites are the span's only disclosure objects.

items.claim: The mid-verse placement of the burden-word is byte-true, but the directional construal the row builds its boundary on is unsupported by the bytes and contradicted by the row's own bounds.
items.evidence: הַמַּשָּׂ֥א הַזֶּֽה closes oshb:Isa.14.28 as the sixth and seventh of that verse's seven tokens (byte tier), so the non-initial placement the row asserts is correct and the site is properly held apart from the verse-initial headers (sweep: 10 verse-initial header verses, this not among them). The defect is the ground the row states for its boundary: it reads the demonstrative as backward-pointing to the burden it dates, and nothing in the bytes supports the reversal. The identical noun-plus-demonstrative construction הַמָּשָׁ֥ל הַזֶּ֛ה at oshb:Isa.14.4 (byte tier) points forward to the speech that follows it, and this row's own span places the dated burden after the notice, so the stated construal argues against the decision it is offered to support — the boundary and its rationale point opposite ways. The boundary itself is otherwise well corroborated (PE seg after Isa.14.27, SAMEKH seg after Isa.14.32, single witness, tier-3, types kept apart in the row's prose), but the row's signal key merges petuchah and setumah into one label, against the standing rule that the two mark types are never conflated.

items.claim: The row's own opening-seam driver sits inside an undisclosed ketiv/qere verse whose variant changes the addressee, and the span's woe-family token is left unverified.
items.evidence: Four of the five imperatives the row names as the driver of its opening seam and of its addressee-continuity argument stand in oshb:Isa.16.3 — one of the 49 variant-note verses, staged as a DOUBLED token pair at the very head of that chain: הביאו (ketiv, unpointed in the extract — skeleton grade only, not quotation grade) beside הָבִ֤יאִי (qere, byte tier). The two differ precisely in addressee: the ketiv carries the masculine-plural imperative ending, the qere the feminine-singular, and the rest of the chain alternates in the pointed bytes — עֲשׂ֣וּ masculine plural against שִׁ֧יתִי, סַתְּרִי֙ and תְּגַלִּֽי feminine singular (all byte tier). The row asserts continuity of the appeal's addressee across Isa.16.1-Isa.16.5 in order to hold the throne promise inside the unit, so the one layer that directly contests that claim is the one layer it never discloses, and any count or slice in this verse also meets the doubled token. The English of both witnesses cannot show the alternation (an undifferentiated second person), so the continuity reading is translation-carried, not byte-carried. Separately, הֱוִי at oshb:Isa.16.4 (byte tier) is skeleton-identical to the book's woe particle but is pointed with hataf-segol and hiriq against the holam-pointed ה֤וֹי of the particle (oshb:Isa.55.1, byte tier) — an imperative of the verb 'to be', not a woe onset. The row engages no woe-family signal, leaving the only span-internal token that could have marked a tier-1 seam inside its own bounds unverified. The parashah layer owes nothing here (no seg falls in Isa.16.1-Isa.16.5).

items.claim: The row's only mark citation is oriented backwards: the seg it calls the unit's opening stands one verse later, inside the span, at exactly the interior seam the row denies.
items.evidence: In the single witness the SAMEKH seg attached to Isa.16.6 stands after that verse's words and before Isa.16.7's opening, so it marks a break at Isa.16.6|Isa.16.7 — not at Isa.16.5|Isa.16.6. The row's claim that a setumah opens the unit at Isa.16.6 inverts the orientation the same span's other four mark citations apply correctly, where the segs standing after Isa.14.2, Isa.14.23, Isa.14.27 and Isa.14.32 are each read as closing their verse. The mark type is right and the single-witness disclosure is present, so the defect is the located role, not the citation. The consequence is substantive rather than cosmetic: the row's rejected alternative denies any seam between Isa.16.6 and Isa.16.12, while the break the cited seg actually corroborates falls at the לָכֵ֗ן onset of oshb:Isa.16.7 (byte tier), immediately after the report opening שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ גְאוֹן מוֹאָ֖ב at oshb:Isa.16.6 (byte tier) — an interior signal the row leaves undisclosed while citing the very layer that carries it. This weak single-witness layer cannot drive the boundary in either direction, but the corroboration as stated is byte-false.
